properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-10-07: linking across the one design "may also help prevent duplicate decisions/ideas/requirements/capabilities or issues in proper separation of concerns. I think we've also discussed and may have made a requirement that a design pushes requirements/decisions to the lowest project level and that becomes the 'single source of truth' for the whole project."

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, AND IS NOT REOPENED HERE:
- req:a-skill-run-in-a-session-holding-several-designs-writes-where-the-fact-belongs (accepted 2026-09-22, from his words "any fact only appears 'once'... should be at the lowest level"): a writing skill puts a fact in the lowest design that owns all of it. Realized as the /hub skill's routing step, which is text an agent must follow. fact:root-cause-a-writing-skill-in-a-multi-design-session-never-reached-the-routing-step-2026-10-04 measured it missed three times.
- req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design (accepted, advisory, not built). Per dec:until-designs-share-a-server-the-cross-design-check-runs-at-the-hub (2026-09-28) it waits until designs share a server; meanwhile the check is one search across the hub and its designs, read before writing (req:one-search-reaches-every-design-a-hub-tracks, planned).
- dec:idea-a-contract-is-declared-at-the-lowest-level-and-rolled-up (accepted): contracts at the lowest level that defines them, answered higher up by roll-up.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: everything above acts at the moment of writing. Nothing looks at what is ALREADY in the family: a requirement the hub holds that only one child acts on, the same decision in two siblings, a capability in the parent that a part realizes. Those accumulate from before the routing existed, from the misses above, and from adopt over existing projects (dec:idea-how-does-a-hub-learn-two-of-its-projects-duplicate-or-contradict-each-other).

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) WRITE TIME ONLY, as settled. Nothing new.
(b) A FAMILY SWEEP the hub runs on demand: candidate duplicates, and facts held higher than needed (a parent node whose every link lands in one child), put to the owner as questions, never moved automatically. Medium. It rests on one search across designs (planned) and on a cross-design relation to record the verdict (dec:idea-a-relation-between-nodes-in-two-designs-is-recorded-so-linking-works-on-the-one-design).
(c) THE HOST RUNS THE SWEEP for hosted families (flo2's dec:idea-flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-design-graph-when-asked).

COUNTERPOINTS:
- Cross-design similarity across different vocabularies is unreliable; the 09-22 ruling kept the write warning advisory for that reason, and a sweep inherits the same false-alarm rate in bulk.
- "Held too high" is a judgement: a hub legitimately holds what spans its children (req:a-design-over-the-parts-of-one-thing-holds-what-no-part-owns), and a requirement may sit in the parent BECAUSE it is the whole's.
- Moving a fact between designs is a write in two designs with two owners, so the fix is always a question, never an action.
properties.name: OPEN — should a family of designs be CHECKED, after the fact, for the same thing held twice, or held higher than the lowest design that owns it (separation of concerns), rather than relying only on the routing at write time?
properties.rationale: The one-home rule is enforced only at the moment of writing, by an agent following text, and that has been measured to miss. A periodic look at the whole family is the backstop the write-time rule does not have.
